name: Polynucleotide eye filler

lead: Polynucleotide eye filler is an injection of polynucleotide-based product into the thin skin around the eyes, aimed at better-quality, smoother, less crepey skin rather than adding large volume.

Proponents describe polynucleotides as stimulating skin repair and hydration. Very little documentation exists for the periorbital use; a registered observational study of a periorbital rejuvenation procedure (n=29) does not name the product.

paras: It is done as a clinic injection treatment, and the aim is gradual skin improvement rather than an immediate contour change.

Injections near the eye carry the general risks of periorbital injectables, including bruising, swelling and lumpiness, and the thin skin shows irregularities. No specific safety data for this use were found.

angle.text: Polynucleotide injections around the eyes aim to improve skin quality, so thin, crepey lower-lid skin looks smoother and fresher over time. Very little published research covers this eye-area use.

lead: Polynucleotide eye filler is a name for injections of polynucleotide-based products into the thin skin of the lower eyelid and surrounding area, intended to improve the quality of periorbital skin.

The sources reviewed contain almost no published evidence on this use. One registered prospective, non-interventional study of a periorbital rejuvenation procedure (n=29, completed 2025) lists glabellar lines, midface volume deficiency and periorbital wrinkling as conditions, but the listing does not identify the product used [1].

paras: No studies found. A registered non-interventional study assessing a periorbital rejuvenation procedure enrolled 29 participants, but the registration does not name polynucleotides [1].
